ai.description: The Himalayan Toad reaches 10–15 cm. It is dark brown or olive with prominent, kidney-shaped parotoid glands and a distinct, bony cranial crest behind the eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Himalayan Toad is best distinguished by its prominent, continuous cranial crests that form a distinct "L" shape behind the eyes, meeting the enlarged, kidney-shaped parotoid glands.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Toad inhabits moist temperate forests and alpine meadows across the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 3,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for insects and invertebrates across the damp, high-altitude terrain of its mountainous habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Himalayan Toad breeds in pools and streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying thousands of eggs in long, gelatinous strings typical of the genus *Duttaphrynus*.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalayan Toad occurs across the Himalayas in India, spanning states like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim at elevations between 1,500 and 3,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Himalayan Toad emits a low-pitched, rhythmic trill consisting of a series of rapid, pulsed notes, typically heard near mountain streams and moist forest habitats.
